cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Monogamy – the practice or state of having a relationship with only one partner at a time.

p.em: Example: She wondered if her unwavering loyalty to old family customs was a form of cultural monogamy.

cosy-blockquote.p: Monopoly – exclusive possession or control of the supply of or trade in a commodity or service.

p.em: Example: The traditional wedding industry holds a near monopoly on how we define romantic success.

cosy-blockquote.p: Devotion – love, loyalty, or enthusiasm for a person, activity, or cause.

p.em: Example: His absolute devotion to the family reunion was both touching and slightly exhausting.

cosy-blockquote.p: Heirloom – a valuable object that has belonged to a family for several generations.

p.em: Example: The heavy gold watch was a precious family heirloom that carried decades of silent expectations.

cosy-blockquote.p: Unwavering – steady or resolute; not wavering or showing hesitation.

p.em: Example: Despite their differences, the community maintained an unwavering support for the annual harvest festival.

cosy-blockquote.p: Arbitrary – based on random choice or personal whim, rather than any reason or system.

p.em: Example: Many of our most beloved holidays are based on completely arbitrary calendar dates.

cosy-blockquote.p: Preserve – to maintain something in its original or existing state.

p.em: Example: Older generations fight desperately to preserve customs that younger people find irrelevant.

cosy-blockquote.p: Anachronistic – belonging or appropriate to a period other than that in which it exists.

p.em: Example: In our digital age, writing physical letters can feel delightfully anachronistic.

cosy-blockquote.p: Reverence – deep respect for someone or something.

p.em: Example: She treated her grandmother's recipes with a level of reverence usually reserved for sacred texts.

cosy-blockquote.p: Customary – according to the customs or usual practices associated with a particular society.

p.em: Example: It is customary to bring a small gift when visiting a host in traditional communities.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Why do we feel a deep sense of devotion to customs we didn't choose, while struggling to commit to modern relationships?
★ Complete using inversion: 'Seldom do people question inherited cultural traditions before accepting them.'

Is following an anachronistic tradition a form of comforting stability or a lazy refusal to define our own values?
★ What is the oldest family heirloom or ritual you own, and what does it mean to you?

Does society exercise a strict monopoly over our personal milestones through traditional wedding and career timelines?
★ Have you ever chosen to ignore a customary life milestone to pursue your own unique path?

Can we show genuine reverence for our heritage without pledging an unwavering loyalty that stifles personal growth?
★ Is there a specific ritual from your childhood that you still preserve with absolute care?

In what ways do family expectations turn cultural habits into a mandatory monogamy, where exploring alternative lifestyles is seen as a betrayal?
★ Have you ever felt like a rebel just for wanting to try a non-traditional way of celebrating a holiday?

When we blindly inherit a family heirloom belief system, are we respecting our ancestors or simply letting dead people rule our lives?
★ Do you find yourself showing reverence for old habits even when they no longer serve a practical purpose?

Why is it customary to feel guilty when we skip a traditional family gathering in favor of personal solitude?
★ How do you handle family members who demand unwavering attendance at every traditional event?

If we treat our cultural habits with the same commitment as marital monogamy, does that make other cultures' rituals seem like infidelity?
★ Have you ever felt drawn to another culture's holiday rituals more than your own?

Is the urge to preserve outdated rules a way to cope with the chaotic, unpredictable nature of modern life?
★ What is one modern habit you hope will become a customary ritual for future generations?

How do we differentiate between a comforting custom that brings people together and an arbitrary rule that keeps us separated?
★ In your opinion, does the pressure of social conformity create a monopoly on how we define happiness?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
Traditional societies derived their identity from a singular, lifelong devotion to collective rituals, whereas modern urbanites continuously cycle through fleeting, self-made trends.
★ Do you find comfort in modern flexibility, or do you sometimes crave the steady, predefined role of traditional societies?

Older generations passed down a physical family heirloom as a symbol of continuity, while modern citizens define their legacy through ephemeral digital archives.
★ If you had to choose, would you rather inherit a physical antique or a collection of written family memoirs?

While past eras enforced a strict, customary timeline for marriage and child-rearing, modern life offers an endless buffet of choices that leads to chronic decision paralysis.
★ Have you ever felt overwhelmed by the sheer number of lifestyles available to you today compared to your parents' youth?

Ancient communities treated their local customs as an absolute monopoly on truth, whereas modern multicultural cities force us to constantly negotiate our values.
★ Do you enjoy living in a culturally diverse environment, or do you sometimes wish for a simpler, more uniform community?

Traditional life relied on unwavering commitment to the soil and neighborhood, while modern globalization turns us into geographic nomads who struggle to establish deep roots.
★ Have you lived in multiple cities, and if so, how has that constant movement affected your sense of belonging?

In the past, showing reverence for ancestral authority was the foundation of social order, but modern culture celebrates the rebellious disruptor who breaks old rules.
★ Who is the most non-conformist person you know, and do you admire their willingness to challenge established customs?

Traditional marital monogamy was often a pragmatic economic contract, whereas modern romance is a highly romanticized quest for individual self-actualization.
★ Do you think modern romance is more fragile because we expect our partners to be our lovers, best friends, and therapists all at once?

Outdated, anachronistic laws were once protected in the name of sacred tradition, whereas modern secular societies are more willing to discard outdated rules to maximize individual liberty.
★ What is one old social norm that you are glad has been largely discarded by modern society?

While past generations fought desperately to preserve ancestral structures, modern capitalism prioritizes rapid development and constant demolition.
★ Do you feel sad when old buildings or natural landscapes in your city are replaced by modern steel skyscrapers?

Traditional systems created a comforting but rigid social structure, whereas modern freedom has left many feeling utterly liberated yet deeply isolated.
★ Would you rather trade some of your individual freedom for a guarantee of a tight-knit, supportive local community?
